title: Lane C P1: Provider Capability Spine and Gemini Inference Admission Closure
summary: Implemented canonical provider capability classification vocabulary distinguishing direct inference providers from routed gateways, local runtimes, and external harnesses. Closed the configured-but-unresolvable Gemini inference admission gap by implementing a native Gemini adapter (GeminiAdapter + GeminiMapper) conforming to the existing APIAdapter Protocol, wired into the adapter resolution path. Added a read-only provider capability inspection surface. Delivered 31 new tests; 113 pass. Gemini now resolves through _get_adapter('gemini') without KeyError.

sections.content: ProviderClass distinguishes architectural role from API protocol style. DeepSeek using an OpenAI-compatible protocol is classified as direct_inference (not OpenAI). OpenRouter is classified as routed_gateway (not direct_inference), with a note recording that downstream provider provenance is not yet captured. A2A provider profiles remain external harness records and are not inference-provider records.

Causal proofs delivered by tests: (1) Anthropic direct inference ≠ Claude Code external harness — A2A provider_profiles module remains untouchable by inference models. (2) OpenAI direct inference class name ≠ Responses API style name — ProviderClass.DIRECT_INFERENCE is distinct from api_style='openai'. (3) OpenRouter gateway identity preserved despite OpenAI-compatible protocol — get_provider_class('openrouter') returns ROUTED_GATEWAY, not DIRECT_INFERENCE. (4) Ollama local runtime classified as local_server class; any future Ollama Cloud record would use cloud_offloaded_local — ProviderClass enum has the value but no execution code exists.

sections.content: compute_provider_capabilities() returns a list of ProviderCapability records for all 6 registered providers. No network calls, no secret exposure, no inference, no persistence mutation. The surface answers: which provider classes exist, which provider/model combinations are configured, which capabilities are verified for a model, whether a provider is direct/gateway/local/harness, and whether a configured provider is executable now. It does not select models, initiate inference, spend money, persist telemetry, mutate configuration, expose secrets, create A2A tasks, or reach into desktop/analytics surfaces. Verified by test_read_surface_performs_no_network_calls (idempotent output) and test_capability_records_contain_no_secrets (no 'sk-' prefix in any capability record field).

sections.content: (1) Gemini multi-turn conversation handling: the adapter maps LLMMessage to Gemini contents array with system_instruction extraction, but the Gemini API places constraints on role alternation (user/model/user...) that may not be satisfied by arbitrary message histories. (2) Max token handling: the adapter sets maxOutputTokens on generationConfig, but Gemini's exact max_output behaviour differs from OpenAI — future use may need model-specific tuning. (3) The existing DEFAULT_PROVIDERS list includes a 'google' ProviderConfig that now uses api_style='gemini' — any user-customized config toml files that set api_style='google' will still fail with KeyError until they update to 'gemini'. Migration note in audit artifact serves as documentation.

lane_c_p1_provider_capability_gemini_closure_proven — All 31 new tests pass. Gemini configured-but-unresolvable KeyError gap closed. Canonical ProviderClass vocabulary delivered. Read-only capability inspection surface available for downstream routing policy, desktop projections, and A2A admission. No cross-lane authority violations.
